After breakfast, meet your guide at 08:00 and transfer to the border with El Salvador. A local guide will help you with immigration formalities before you continue to your hotel in San Salvador.

In the afternoon, take a tour of the capital. You’ll see the historic centre, its main sights and squares, and visit the cathedral, the craft market and the relief map of San Salvador. The viewpoint looks out over the city.

Overnight at La-Terraza Hotel in San Salvador.
Monumental stone building with towers beside a street in Guatemala City, Guatemala
Guatemala City: a long stone façade with towers and arched windows
Joya de Cerén – San Andrés – Tazumal

After breakfast, meet your guide at 08:00 and travel to Joya de Cerén. A cultural heritage site since 1993, it preserves original Maya settlements that lay buried under volcanic ash for more than 1,400 years. You can see how their inhabitants went about daily life.

Next, visit the archaeological area of San Andrés, an important ceremonial centre where the first indigo production factory was discovered.

Your next stop is the ruins of Tazumal, the most important Maya site in El Salvador. The name Tazumal, also spelled Tatzumal, means “pyramid where the victims were burned” in K’iche’. The complex was built in 13 stages over 750 years, mainly in the Late Classic period, between AD 600 and 900. Archaeologists believe the earliest settlements in the area date to around the fifth millennium BC.

Return to San Salvador in the evening.

Overnight at La-Terraza Hotel.
